A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpineMed-450k, SpineBench, and SpineGPT work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, training-data ablations, human-expert agreement results, and a clinical case comparison.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds Medgemma-27B evaluations, a spine-only training ablation, and benchmark distribution analyses.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 adds a separate GPT-5-mini semantic-consistency filter after Picture Context Matching to reject mismatched image-context pairs. This extends the described curation procedure; the Qwen2.5-VL-7B architecture and three-stage curriculum remain unchanged. Naming previously unspecified generation models is additional implementation disclosure.

E1.justification: The training sources, orthopedic domains, languages, imaging modalities, and evaluation tasks remain unchanged. Appendix F describes the existing benchmark population. The additional datasets discussed in v3 Table 1 are descriptive comparisons, not newly used training or evaluation datasets.

E2.justification: Medgemma-27B is added to the main comparison and detailed report-generation comparison in v3 Tables 6 and 9; it was cited but absent from the corresponding v1 Tables 4 and 7. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The reported maximum sequence lengths for training stages 1 and 2 change from 16,284 in v1 Table 6 to 16,384 in v3 Table 5, without establishing that experiments were rerun. v3 also adds a spine-only training control. The 487-question and 87-report evaluation sets, scoring rubrics, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 Table 7 adds a spine-only ablation that isolates the contribution of spinal instruction data beyond the existing general-medical and non-spine controls. Appendix F adds descriptive disease and source analyses to assess benchmark representativeness. The expert-agreement analysis and clinical case study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for model performance. The Pearson-correlation analysis in Figure 5 is unchanged; the added distribution tables do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing model scores remain unchanged, including SpineGPT's reported overall score of 87.44. v3 adds Medgemma-27B results and spine-only ablation scores of 87.76 text, 86.01 image, and 87.07 average, plus benchmark distribution entries. Some additions are inconsistent: Medgemma's risk-prognosis score is 4.14 in Table 6 but 3.26 in Table 9.

T1.justification: The scoring definitions and Equations 1–3 remain unchanged. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs, and v3 adds no new formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a large level-aware instruction corpus, a clinician-designed benchmark, weaknesses in existing models, and improved performance through specialized fine-tuning.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the spine-only ablation as evidence that spinal instruction data is decisive and the Medgemma comparison as showing insufficient specialization from medical pretraining alone. It adds parameter-efficiency and safe local-deployment arguments, representativeness and zero-leakage assertions, and explicit redistribution constraints. The original limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 substantially revises the promised release from making every project component available to a tiered arrangement: open instruction annotations and code, pointers to externally obtained images, and a controlled-access clinical subset requiring a data-use agreement. It also identifies the curation models, eight A100 GPUs, ms-swift, and processing safeguards. These materially clarify reproducibility requirements, although the PDFs do not establish completed releases.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 and Table 1 expand comparisons with perception-focused spine datasets, including RSNA LumbarDISC, BUU-LSPINE, and Lumbar Spine MRI. Appendix C develops these comparisons and adds general-vision citations. The existing positioning around specialized, multimodal clinical reasoning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 separates SpineGPT implementation and curriculum into a dedicated section, reorders expert agreement and ablations, and reorganizes the appendices with a contents page. Ethics and reproducibility passages are rewritten and relocated, and author information is revised. Most scientific prose and all retained prompt text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds dataset-comparison, data-governance, and benchmark-distribution tables, expands existing result tables, and moves the reformatted training table into the main text. Conference headers and float placement change, while the existing figures, clinical-report panels, and prompt displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The spine-only control and clearer implementation and access documentation improve interpretability and reproducibility. However, new Table 10 percentages total 84.85% despite a stated 100% total, and Medgemma's risk-prognosis scores conflict between Tables 6 and 9. Added safety and zero-leakage assertions also lack corresponding validation. These weaknesses undermine parts of the new evidence, leaving the net quality effect uncertain.
